title: A label set to stretch does something you can see
goal: In the new Layout section you can tell a piece to stretch, and a piece of text will take the setting and then look identical, because its box gets wider and its words stay where they were. Either the words should sit somewhere sensible in the box they now fill, or text should say plainly that stretching is not for it.
notes: From the placement audit 2026-09-03 (queue/audits/2026-09-03-ui-components-placement.json). Today Stretch widens the layer frame and TextRasterizer draws at the natural size from the frame origin, so nothing visibly moves. Real reflow is auto layout (ui-layout, staged later), so the short version here is probably a text alignment inside the frame, or hiding Stretch for text content.
acceptance: Setting a text layer to Stretch either moves its words in a way you can see, or the choice is not offered for text and the row says why
Whatever is chosen, a label that was centred in a button is still centred after the button is resized
The design doc records the decision

log.note: Adversarial pre-review. Walked it as a first-timer: select the word inside a Button, Layout > Horizontal > Stretch. The box widens and the glyphs do not move, because the app has no idea where words sit inside their own box: TextRasterizer always draws from the top left. So the missing thing is not stretch, it is text alignment, which this app has never had at all (you cannot centre a caption over a picture today except by dragging it by eye). Rejected the cheap option of hiding Stretch for text: a WRAPPED paragraph already reflows when its box widens (the rasterizer wraps to the frame), which is exactly what a card body wants, so hiding it would remove the one thing that works. Shortest version that delivers the value: give text an Align (words across, words down), honour it in the rasterizer, and have Stretch set Align to Center/Middle when the text has none of its own, so the choice does something the moment it is made and the Layout row can say so in words. Cut: justified text, per-paragraph controls, any reflow of point size (that is auto layout's job).

Core + renderer landed, TDD. TextContent carries an optional alignment and verticalAlignment (nil = the top left every older document drew at, no key written); TextRasterizer honours both (a paragraph style across, a shortened lay-out box down, and a box too small for the words keeps every line by drawing exactly what it always drew); setPlacement on a text layer with stretch on an axis sets Center/Middle on that axis when the words have never been placed, in the same one edit. 27 rasterizer tests + 12 new core tests green.

App layer landed: an Align row (two segmented controls, words across and words down) in the Text section behind next-placement; the Layout section's caption for a stretched piece of text says the box fills and Align places the words; re-editing text keeps a box bigger than its words at that width and types the draft in the alignment it will commit to, so a centred label does not spring left mid-edit. Decision written into docs/design/ui-building.md as 'Where the words sit in their box'. Full suite green (2364 tests).

Reviewed on the real app (probe, Screen Recording granted): Scripts/playtest/stretched-words-walk.json, 56 steps, ok. Verified acceptance 1: setting Stretch on a text layer flips the Align row to Center and adds a line saying what stretch means for words, and the next resize stretches the box and carries the words to the middle of it (words-3-wider-sc.png shows the word 130 points right of where it was pinned before). Honest caveat: nothing on the canvas moves at the MOMENT of the pick, which is true of every Layout rule, so the visible proof is one drag away. Acceptance 2: a label centred in a button is still centred at any width, both through the button's own Center rule (unchanged) and through stretch+Center (covered by aStretchedLabelStaysCentred). Acceptance 3: docs/design/ui-building.md, 'Where the words sit in their box'. Audit written to queue/audits/2026-09-03-stretched-words.json with three real screenshots. Also filed a-screen-repaints-its-surface-as-soon-as-it-is-r: during the walk the frame's painted surface stayed the old size in the window while the offscreen render of the same step was right.
